description: Seven transfers that must be refused. Four are about the amount, because the amount is the field most often wrong in a real feed and the one whose errors survive longest.

cases.name: zero_amount
cases.why: A zero transfer is not an event. It would be counted in every transfer-count feature while contributing nothing to any value feature, which is a velocity signal with no money behind it.

cases.name: negative_amount
cases.why: Direction is carried by the sender and receiver columns, not by the sign. A negative amount would be summed as a negative inflow and could cancel a real one, producing a throughput of nearly zero for an account with heavy traffic.

cases.name: amount_with_thousands_separators
cases.why: '24,000.00' is what a spreadsheet export produces. It is refused rather than parsed, because the comma is a decimal separator in much of the world and guessing which one it is here would be a factor-of-a-hundred error in a monetary figure.

cases.name: amount_without_currency
cases.why: Defaulted rather than refused, and listed here because the default is the interesting part: the configured default currency is applied and a caveat is recorded. Per-currency totals are never summed, so an amount filed under the wrong currency is invisible rather than wrong -- it just stops appearing in the total it belongs to.
cases.expected: accepted with a defaulted currency and a caveat

cases.name: missing_reference
cases.why: reference is required and unique. It is how a complaint naming a transaction is matched to one, which is the entirety of tier-1 correlation -- the only tier that needs no confidence score and no human review.

cases.name: unknown_sender_account
cases.why: Both account columns are foreign keys. An unknown sender must fail rather than being created, because an account conjured from a transfer has no opening date, type or status, and would score as a brand-new account forever.

cases.name: channel_outside_the_vocabulary
cases.why: CHEQUE has no value in the channel enum and no honest alias. The normalizer maps a source system's wording where the meaning is unambiguous -- WIRE to NEFT, INSTANT to IMPS -- and refuses where it is not, rather than filing the record under the nearest-looking rail.
